comment: Professor Simon is a passionate professor who cares about his students. The class is very reasonable. Homework is extremely minimal with about 10 pages of reading for each class. This reading is expected and there are pop quizzes weekly based on those readings which are also very manageable. I highly recommend taking the class.

Professor Simon is a great professor. He encourages critical thinking and thought-provoking observations. He does random pop quizzes, which are usually easy if you did the reading. He emphasizes class participation, and it's not hard usually to participate. Two exams and one final. Very nice guy to speak to after classes if you have any questions.

I liken Dr. Simon to an incredibly knowledgeable, congenial, and respected grandfather you always wish you could spend more time with. His classes (both 333 and 339) are high-quality seminar-style illustrations of the value inherent in a quality liberal arts education - informative and thought-provoking. I cannot recommend him or his classes more.

he is super sweet and kind and doesn't assign much reading and the pop quizzes are super easy if you read before. his lectures are insightful and the two midterms and final are essays that are easy if you know the cases

Class is a typical Socratic seminar and is guided by the students; he challenges you to think & defend yourself; you tackle a lot of political philosophers & moral dilemmas; tests are all digital timed writes; lots of pop quizzes; strongly recommend you take extensive notes & do not skip the readings

Simon is an outstanding professor with evident expectations in everything. He is very orderly and fair, with a clear passion for the subject he teaches. He does pop quizzes, which aren't too bad if you do the readings. He encourages participation, self-reflection, and interpretation with the material.

I loved this class and liked Dr. Simon. I thought our discussions were engaging and I never felt annoyed to be sitting in his class. The lectures are not the most engaging on their own but if you commit to them, they can be. The tests are very easy and the quizzes are easy if you simply do the readings--which are 10 pages long each class (light)

Prof. Simon does an amazing job with the courses he teaches. His class style is very laid-back and engaging, where lectures often wander yet remain strangely on-topic - in a remarkably productive way.  All you have to do is read, think, and synthesize on tests. He's super supportive and loves to hear what his students think. Would 100% take again.

Simon was one of the best profs. here at UR. His exams are super easy as long as you know the court cases and all you have to do is read before the pop quizzes now and then and participate. Super nice and understanding. Take him.

Professor Simon is a really great professor and a great person in general. He cares about what he teaches and tries to work through the material in a way that students can understand, though there is a LOT of content to cover. He is easily accessible outside of class and also cares a lot about students' concerns

Dr. Simon is a really good professor! I learned a lot in his 339 course, though I felt it was much more oriented toward philosophy than political science, so anticipate that going in. Routine quizzes were pretty straight forward and based on the readings, and tests were generally fair though not always an easy A.

Dr. Simon is a great guy, and a good professor. The course is much more philosophy heavy than political science heavy, but is interesting nonetheless. Feedback on exams is very timely, and he is super accommodating to students regarding meeting outside of class or getting extra help. Lectures are strictly discussion based, with not much structure.

Really nice and knows a lot about the topic. Lectures are a bit all over, with no clear structure. Not a lot of exam preperation either, so you mostly rely on your notes from lecture. Definitely more phil than poli-sci and very confusing/dense readings. The class is interesting but I don't know if the difficulty is worth taking it.

A really nice guy & an overall good prof. Not a lot of homework, which is nice. But class seems unnecessarily harder than it needs to be. He is a really tough grader on exams & gives too many pop quizzes. The course is more philosophy than polisci - there isn't much of any connection with American politics as it advertises. Will not help your GPA.

Professor Simon is a great guy, and I overall enjoyed my time in class with him. He likes to give short pop quizzes about once a week, but it was beneficial because it held everyone accountable for each reading (which was not too long). The class is lecture-heavy and sometimes got confusing because of the nature of the topics we were discussing.

On a normal day, Dr. Simon would walk in, hand out a pop quiz, and five minutes later start the lecture. He was very passionate about the subject, and he gave brilliant explanations. 100% would recommend.

Great guy, but lecture heavy class that can be (very) boring. Hardish grader depending on how much work you're willing to put in. Reading quizzes almost every class so you have to actually take time to understand material. Otherwise the class is fairly straightforward & not graded on much- a couple essays and in class midterm.

Prof. Simon's just fabulous. Excellent at conveying abstractions and why they deserve consideration, rather than simply reveling in them for their own sake. Realistic in his expectations, and appeared to have motivated my peers to a similar extent relative to other professors of pol. science and otherwise. Interesting and accessible readings.

Dr. Simon is truly passionate about the subject and it shows. I really enjoyed his "Why Does Anything Exist" class because of the focus on discussion aspect. There were only two papers but a lot of pop quizzes off the reading. At times, the reading was difficult, so be sure to put in time and work.

Professor Simon is so intelligent. He really does care about his students and wants to see them succeed. Participation matters and you have to do the reading to understand what's going on in class discussions and to do well on the daily quizzes. Going to Professor Simons office hours and extra help sessions are super helpful!!!

Probably my favorite professor at Richmond. Genuinely caring and his classes are interesting. Sets clear expectations for students, and super willing to help. He is very welcoming of many opinions. I respect him a lot, as a professor and a person.
Very good professor and very interested in the topic of the course. Discussions were well-led. Reading quizzes almost every day gets a little exhausting.

He's very caring and accomodating and understands the time management struggles of college; nice guy. He doesn't set much reading, but MAKE SURE YOU DO IT as HE WILL QUIZ YOU! Some of the course content was very challenging to understand but he does a relatively good job of unpacking it once you get to class. Expect to write a lot of papers!

Dr. Simon is the kindest and most accommodating professor ever. His fys is truly interesting and he really wants everyone to learn and enjoy the material. Will go through a paprr with you and his points are always valid. Do the readings cuz he gives a quiz every other class. But he is so chill and makes u truly interested in the material

Dr. Simon is one of the best professors I've taken at UR. He's absolutely brilliant and explains the material very clearly. His homework assignments are short and to the point, but he makes sure that you read them thoroughly. The one potentially bad thing about this class is that the midterm and final combined make up 70% of the final grade.

Professor Simon works to help his students. His reading assignments are very manageable, because he expects you to really think about the material. Classes are basically all discussion which is interesting and engaging. His office hours are a great chance to get to know him and understand the course even more.
Fair professor, you really have to earn your grade.

Dr. Simon is really interested in his topic and he's good at facilitating discussion. Pop quizzes are a once a week thing, but they're easy if you did the (always short) reading. Tough essay grader, but fair.
Went to Harvard, grades us like we're at Harvard.

Incredibly passionate and a good guy. Tough to do well without participating. Gives a quiz a week but it's really just a reading check. The readings are all very short and you'll be expected to really digest them before class. Must take.

I love Simon, hands down my favorite professor this semester, possibly ever. I'm taking a class with him next semester just to have him again. He's young and makes you really interested in the Constitution(which could be really hard), grades fairly and makes helpful comments. I'm actually always excited to go to class and listen to the disscusions!

Great Professor for Civil Rights and Liberties. He's young so he knows the proper amount of work to give to not overload you. 20 pages of readina week! Class is interesting and the material is enjoyable to read. Do the wiork and you'll get the grade, he's very fair.
